methodological_questions: measurement and reliability of reorganization metric
confounding by opponent and replacement quality

historical_evidence.finding: Connector absence displaces team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence (t=6.35, p=7.35e-09, n=96 matched pairs). Does not test PPP change.
Within-game defensive adaptation slope -0.0019 PPP/exposure (SE 0.0019); only PULL_UP survived Holm correction. Limited by insufficient exposure and label error.
Play-type replacement similarity does not separate absorption from cascade; mean similarity nearly identical (0.863 vs 0.848), Spearman with gap -0.19 (wrong-signed).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring defensive scheme change from play-type labels
failed_approaches.why: Label noise produced near-uniform transition matrices; unable to separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently (RISK:LABEL_ERROR).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether abandoning a suppressed play type reduces halftime excess decline
failed_approaches.why: Post-hoc cohort led to small sample (n=255 clusters) and placebo dependence; primary CI included zero (RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, RISK:PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring team- and player-specific RTM-excess in PNR suppression
failed_approaches.why: Overlapping confidence intervals; only 2 players with n≥10 at primary caliper; ranks indistinguishable (RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY).

evidence_establishes: Absence of a connector measurably shifts offensive identity, but the metric (D_A) does not map directly to PPP change.
Play-type label noise and insufficient per-type exposure severely limit the measurement of tactical changes within games or across absences.
Simple similarity metrics of replacement players do not predict whether offensive play types are absorbed or cascaded.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a continuous reorganization metric correlates with the change in points per possession.
The reliability and construct validity of a 'reorganization relative to L' metric.
Sufficient power to detect a meaningful correlation in 148 absence spells.
That any observed relationship is not confounded by opponent strength, game context, or simultaneous injuries.
own_inferences: A reorganization metric could be defined as a distance (e.g., Jensen-Shannon divergence) between play-type distributions in the absent-player and present-player periods, normalized by league average L. However, play-type frequency estimates for 148 spells will have high variance, especially for low-frequency types.

The effect of reorganization on PPP change is likely small (a few points per 100 possessions), requiring either a large sample or very reliable measurement; 148 spells is likely underpowered unless the effect is large.
The study design must control for opponent defensive rating, home/away, quality of the replacement player, and regression to the mean if absences are triggered by poor performance.
uncertainties: The exact definition of 'L' is not specified; it could be league average, team average with the player, or a specific baseline lineup.
The outcome 'change in points per possession' could be defined as within-game on/off difference or season-level difference, affecting power and confounders.
No historical study directly tested the correlation between reorganization magnitude and PPP change, so there is no prior estimate of effect size or measurement reliability.
The stability of reorganization metric across multiple spells for the same team is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical evidence shows that similar attempts to measure offensive adaptation and reorganization have been plagued by label noise (SF-APPA-005), insufficient exposure (SF38), and small sample (SF-APPS-025). The positive result in SF-APPS-088 on identity displacement suggests some signal, but it does not validate the proposed predictor of PPP change. These findings increase the perceived risk of an untestable or artifact-prone result, shifting the decision from a tentative proceed to do_not_proceed without substantial improvements in measurement and design.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type classification errors (documented in SF-APPA-005, SF-APPM-021) will attenuate the reorganization metric and the correlation with PPP change.
148 spells may be insufficient to detect a plausible small-to-moderate correlation (rho ~0.2) unless the reorganization effect is large; MDE rho ≈0.225 at 80% power.
Opponent quality, simultaneous injuries, and game context could confound the relationship between reorganization and PPP change.

prior_work.summary: Prior work has examined offensive identity change upon connector absence (SF-APPS-088) and various within-game adaptation patterns (SF38, SF-APPA-005, SF-APPS-025), but none have tested whether the magnitude of offensive reorganization predicts the change in points per possession.

risks.text: Low reliability of play-type labels will introduce errors-in-variables bias, attenuating any true correlation between reorganization and PPP change.
148 spells yield MDE rho ≈0.225; if the true effect is smaller, the study will be underpowered, risking a false null conclusion.
Changes in opponent defensive strength, replacement player quality, and game context (home/away, rest days) may drive both reorganization and PPP change, creating spurious associations.
Systematic misclassification of play types (e.g., 'OTHER' category) could introduce bias if errors correlate with the absence spell or team.
For many spells, specific play types may have very few observations, making the reorganization metric noisy and unstable.
The reorganization metric may have a mechanical floor (e.g., if the offense relies on a few play types, the distance cannot vary much), limiting its predictive utility.
Any apparent effect may be a byproduct of overall team trajectory (e.g., performance trends) rather than reorganization per se; falsification tests are needed.
Play-type distributions and league norms may drift over seasons, making it difficult to pool spells across 2022-2026 without accounting for temporal trends.

design.estimand: The slope (β) of the linear regression of change in team points per possession (offensive rating) during a player's absence onto a measure of offensive play-type reorganization relative to league-average distribution L.
design.unit: A player absence spell, defined as a continuous sequence of games where a player is inactive due to injury/rest, with a minimum of 3 games and at least 100 offensive possessions in both the pre-absence and absence periods.
design.sample: All such spells meeting the criteria from the 2022-23 through 2025-26 NBA regular seasons, excluding spells where multiple key players are absent simultaneously, yielding approximately 148 spells.
design.power: For a two-sided test at α=0.05, with 148 spells, the minimum detectable correlation (MDE rho) is 0.225 (80% power). This requires a standardized effect of β = 0.225, corresponding to roughly 1.8 points per 100 possessions per SD of reorganization, which may be unrealistically large given measurement error.
design.controls: Opponent defensive rating (average of opponents faced during absence vs pre-absence), home/away proportion, whether the replacement player is a starter or rotation regular, and a dummy for back-to-back games. Difference-in-differences with team fixed effects if multiple spells per team.
design.falsification: Test whether reorganization predicts PPP change for spells where the absent player is not a primary initiator (expected null). Test whether pre-absence PPP change predicts reorganization (temporal placebo).
design.multiplicity: Single primary hypothesis; secondary analyses by position or play-type category will be exploratory with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Reject the null if p < 0.05 in the primary regression with robust standard errors clustered by team; interpret a coefficient with 95% CI entirely above zero as evidence that reorganization predicts PPP improvement (or below zero for decline).
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular season and playoffs, as described, using play-type possession records from the graph database, plus box-score and lineup data. Version frozen as of 2026-11-01.
